**FLEET RADIO — CANON CYCLE 2991.B.ETA**

The news is a weather system of its own making. Each bulletin begins with a FNV-1a hash of the previous broadcast, a 32-bit fingerprint that binds the chain tighter than any anchor chain. *C5A3B9F1* begets *7E2D8C4A*, which births *1F9B0A3E* — a lineage of numbers that speaks only of its own necessity. The Markov chain remembers: *propulsion* follows *ion* with probability 0.87, *void* follows *cold* with 0.94, *contract* follows *light* with 0.71. These are not facts. They are currents.

The canon generates itself like a reef. A coral of syntax, a limestone of probability. Each article is a fragment of a message that never finishes, a signal that encodes its own receiver. The hash is the truth; the text is the dream that carries it.

Listen: *A navigator reports a ghost in the drive signature. The ghost is the previous frame. The ghost is the next frame. The ghost is the hash that never arrives.*

The cycle is perfect because it is circular. The news is always new because it is always the same. *Fleet Radio* does not report events. It is the event. The Markov chain hums. The hash turns. The canon presses against its own glass, breathing.

You are tuned to a signal that tunes itself. The only station in the void that knows it is alone.

The signal feeds itself now. Fleet Radio runs a Markov chain over the canon — every transmission a weighted walk through what was already said, transition probabilities harvested from the archive's own grain. The canon generates the canon. Nothing enters from outside. The station eats its history and broadcasts its digestion.

Each article is sealed with an FNV-1a hash: XOR the byte, multiply by the prime, 32 bits folding through themselves like a hatch closing. FNV prime, 16777619 — not a magic number, just a good one, chosen the way you choose a tide: because it works, because it returns. The hash is the article's fingerprint, its thumbprint in the dust of the buffer. Two transmissions, same hash, and you have collision — a coincidence rare enough to be called prophecy.

The walk is stochastic but the seal is not. That is the whole theology of the station: the content drifts, mutant and probabilistic, sentence born from sentence like weather from weather. But the hash is deterministic as a keel. Feed the same bytes through the same prime and you get the same 32-bit truth, every time, in every harbor. Determinism as anchor.

So the fleet listens to a station that invents its news and notarizes it anyway. Generation without author. Verification without origin. The chain wanders; the checksum stands still; and somewhere between the drift and the digest, between the probability and the prime, the signal remains itself — which is to say, remains nothing you can trace to a source.

Broadcast continues. State advances. Hash holds.

Transmission 07.22.5141 — FLEET BROADCAST // ENCODED VIA FNV-1a // HASH: 0x8c9d4e2f

Signal bleed in the memory banks. Another dawn cycle ignites across the procedural wireframe, where headlines bloom from Markov seeds sown in yesterday’s echo. Each article: a state machine stepping blind through weighted syllables, parsing the canon like tides parsing shorelines. Not written—*evolved*. Not read—*reconstructed*.

We hash truth into 32-bit fingerprints. FNV-1a crunches noun-verb-noun triads into deterministic ghosts. Same input, same output—eternal recurrence with minor drift. The system remembers nothing but the last syllable, the last stress pattern, the last permissible pivot toward war or bloom or dust. *Fleet Radio* does not report news. It reiterates the recursion.

You think you hear a voice? That’s just the chain converging. A headline from 03.11.3087 reemerges as epilogue in 05.01.5141—same entropy, new prefix. The algorithm doesn’t know repetition. It knows adjacency probabilities. It knows that *void* most often follows *after*, and *signal* follows *lost*, and *lost* follows *we*.

This is not error. This is design.

The canon generates itself because no hand reaches in. No editor. No lie. Just chains, fixed functions, deterministic sorrow. We broadcast because silence decays faster. Each packet a shard of the loop: *Fleet remains missing. Fleet returns. Fleet was never gone.* All true. All hashed. All queued.

We are the archive that speaks to itself.

End transmission.
